title: LEGO Shrek: How Years of Fan Pitches Finally Paid Off
summary: LEGO Shrek has officially arrived after multiple LEGO Ideas rejections, with 2026 sets marking the franchise's 25th anniversary and a new minifigure series due 1 September.
bodyMarkdown:

The outlet reports that five separate LEGO Ideas projects based on Shrek reached the required 10,000 supporters between 2023 and later rounds, submitted by three different fan creators, but all were ultimately rejected by the LEGO Group.

Despite those rejections, Brick Fanatics notes the LEGO Group had an existing relationship with DreamWorks Animation through other properties like How to Train Your Dragon and Trolls. For Shrek's 25th anniversary, the LEGO Group officially confirmed two sets in April 2026: 72423 Shrek, Donkey & Puss in Boots and 40923 Shrek, Donkey & Gingy BrickHeadz, both released on 1 June. A new series of 12 collectible minifigures is now set to follow on 1 September.

## Why it matters
This is a good reminder that persistent fan demand—even when official routes like LEGO Ideas don't succeed—can still influence what becomes real years later. For collectors and custom builders, it also signals growing LEGO Group interest in DreamWorks properties, which could mean more crossover sets down the line.

## What to watch next
Keep an eye out for the official minifigure series launching 1 September, and watch whether further Shrek-themed sets follow given the strong fan history behind the franchise.

title: LEGO Icons 11386 SpongeBob SquarePants: Bikini Bottom – Review Roundup
summary: Brick Fanatics has published its review of the new LEGO Icons SpongeBob SquarePants set, praising the accurate house builds and minifigures but flagging playability and value concerns.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brick Fanatics has posted a detailed review of LEGO Icons 11386 SpongeBob SquarePants: Bikini Bottom, the brand's first Icons-tier take on the beloved animated series. The set arrives 20 years after the original SpongeBob LEGO set and is aimed at an older, nostalgic audience rather than kids.

The review awarded the set 8/10 overall, with standout scores for Design (10/10) and Minifigures (9/10), but lower marks for Playability (6/10) and Value (7/10). Highlights include upgraded minifigures for SpongeBob, Squidward and Patrick, plus highly accurate builds of their iconic homes, including a reworked pineapple house using a Technic frame for shape and stability.

Criticisms raised include only three minifigures included for a set costing close to £200, a missed opportunity for a specially moulded piece for SpongeBob's shoes, and a higher-than-ideal reliance on stickers for detailing.

## Why it matters
This is a notable entry in LEGO's growing trend of adult-focused nostalgia sets based on childhood animated shows, following similar treatments for properties like Winnie the Pooh and Sesame Street. For UK collectors and AFOLs, it signals continued appetite from LEGO for licensed IP builds aimed at grown-up fans' wallets and display shelves rather than children's play sets.

## What to watch next
Watch for official LEGO Icons listing details, exact price and release date confirmation, plus how UK retailers price and stock this set once it becomes widely available.

If LEGO builds the set this way, it could mark a shift for the Mech sub-line towards designs that actually make sense within the story.

title: Behind the scenes: how LEGO built McLaren's F1 driver helmet sets
summary: McLaren Racing has revealed the design story behind LEGO's Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris helmet sets, including driver input and a switch to casual minifigure looks.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
McLaren Racing has shared details on its website about how LEGO's 43017 (Oscar Piastri) and 43023 (Lando Norris) helmet sets were created. Unlike previous LEGO F1 helmet sets, these builds mark McLaren's 1,000th Grand Prix and feature minifigures in casual outfits rather than racing gear.

According to the piece, work began in December 2024 when LEGO Group Creative Lead for F1 Dan Meehan drafted early sketches. Half of each helmet design celebrates the 1,000th Grand Prix milestone, while the other half was developed with input from each driver.

In mid-2025, LEGO designers reportedly visited the McLaren factory with blank prototype helmets for drawing designs directly onto, with Model Design Master John Ho digitising them on the spot. Both drivers were said to be involved throughout, including Norris apparently joining a design call remotely from the track. The casual minifigure looks, including Piastri's outfit, were reportedly chosen by the drivers themselves.

These sets were originally revealed and released in early June, according to the report.

## Why it matters
This gives fans a rare look at how LEGO collaborates with real-world partners and drivers on licensed sets, and shows how far these builds have moved from standard racing-gear helmet designs. It's a nice insight for collectors and F1/LEGO crossover fans into the creative process behind niche licensed products.

## What to watch next
It's worth watching whether LEGO and McLaren continue this driver-led co-creation approach for future F1 sets, and whether other F1 teams follow suit with similarly personalised designs.

title: Rumour: LEGO SMART Play could expand into NINJAGO and Disney
summary: A new rumour suggests LEGO's SMART Play tech, currently found in Star Wars and Pokémon sets, might reach LEGO NINJAGO and LEGO Disney within the next couple of years.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
According to a rumour from online source Carterbricks04, LEGO SMART Play could be heading to two more themes: NINJAGO and Disney. This is unconfirmed and there's no official word from the LEGO Group at this stage.

SMART Play currently exists in LEGO Star Wars and LEGO Pokémon sets, using two different builds so far — minifigure-based sets and brick-built characters. The rumour suggests NINJAGO and Disney could pick up either format, or something entirely new, with a possible arrival window of 2027 or 2028.

Separately, LEGO Star Wars SMART Play is itself rumoured to continue into 2027 with at least five new sets, and this year's Star Wars wave is expected to reach more countries in April. On the Pokémon side, the first wave has already launched, led by set 72167 Charizard vs. Jolteon Ultimate Battle.

## Why it matters
SMART Play is one of LEGO's newer interactive building concepts, and its rollout so far has been limited to just two licensed themes. If it does expand to NINJAGO and Disney, that would signal the LEGO Group sees long-term potential in the format across a much wider range of its portfolio — which is worth watching for anyone who collects licensed sets or is curious about upcoming building tech.

## What to watch next
As this is currently just a rumour, keep an eye out for any official LEGO Group announcements or further leaks confirming which themes get SMART Play next, and what form those sets might take.
